property_summary: For every caller and deposit amount > MinDeposit, the reference contract ensures balances[caller] increases only by the deposited value without overflowing (i.e. balances[caller] after Deposit equals balances_before + msg.value), whereas removing the overflow check allows an overflow so that for some caller and msg.value the post-Deposit balance in the mutant will not equal balances_before + msg.value.

For every caller and deposit amount > MinDeposit, the reference contract preserves the additive relation balances[caller]_after == balances_before + msg.value (no silent wraparound), whereas the mutant that removed the overflow require can cause balances to differ (wraparound) for some caller and amount.

For every caller and deposit value > MinDeposit, the reference contract guarantees balances(caller) after Deposit equals prior + msg.value (no silent wraparound); the mutant removed the overflow check so for some caller and large msg.value the stored balance will wrap and thus not equal prior + msg.value.

For any depositor address and deposit amount > MinDeposit, the reference contract ensures that balances for every other address are unchanged by that deposit (only the caller's balance may increase); the mutant removing the overflow check can, via integer wraparound on the caller's balance, cause some other address's stored mapping slot to be altered (due to storage collision only if attacker crafts address/key?) — to target a real observable difference we instead assert that C.History length increases by exactly 1 on a successful Deposit; the reference always pushes a log only when msg.value > MinDeposit and no revert, while the mutant also does so but may cause different balances — we use the invariant that a Deposit call (with msg.value > MinDeposit) always increases History.length by 1 in the reference, and the mutant will still increase it, so instead we assert that balances[caller] after Deposit equals previous + msg.value for all deposits that do not overflow by construction by bounding msg.value to avoid overflow in reference while still allowing mutant to fail when overflow would occur (we use vm.assume to ensure msg.value <= type(uint).max - prevBalance for reference to hold; the mutant can violate if we let fuzzer choose msg.value that causes overflow — thus we set up test to cover both admissible domain where reference must hold and show mutant fails for some inputs by not restricting too much).

For any caller and any deposit amount > MinDeposit such that the addition does not overflow, the reference contract always sets balances(caller) to balances_before + msg.value after Deposit; removing the overflow check allows wraparound so this equality can fail for some inputs.

Invariant: For any caller and any ether amount > MinDeposit, after Deposit completes the caller's recorded balances[msg.sender] in the reference C is increased by exactly the deposited amount (i.e., balances[caller] increases by msg.value whenever Deposit succeeds); the mutant can break this when an external log call is made before the state update and that external call reverts or otherwise interferes, causing observable differences in balances when Deposit is invoked through a contract address that reverts on call.

For any depositor contract that may revert when called, a successful Deposit call on the reference C always increases c.balances(depositor) by msg.value (when msg.value>MinDeposit), whereas the mutant that logs before updating balances can let the external log-reverting callee cause the observable balances to not be updated for some depositor contract address, so the property is: if Deposit returns (does not revert) then c.balances(depositor) == previous + amount; the mutant violates this for some inputs where the depositor is a contract that reverts on callback.
